instructions: Peel both mangoes and cut the flesh off the pits. Dice the flesh of the second mango into small cubes. Put a few cubes in the bottom of each of 4 serving cups and keep the rest for the top.
Blend about 150 g (2/3 cup) of the first mango with 1/4 cup cold water until smooth. Pour it through a fine strainer into a bowl. Stir in the cream and 3 tbsp of the milk.
In a small pot off the heat, stir the agar and sugar into 1/3 cup water. Bring it to a boil over medium heat, stirring, and boil for 2 minutes until you can't see any grains. Take it off the heat.
Pour the agar mixture slowly into the mango mixture, stirring as you pour. Work quickly, since agar starts to set as it cools.
Pour it over the cubes in the cups. If there are bubbles on top, pop them with the tip of a folded paper towel.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours, until set. It keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.
Before serving, pour a thin layer of the remaining 2 tbsp milk over each pudding and top with the mango cubes you saved.
advance_prep_notes: make and chill at least 2 hours ahead, or the day before
method_notes: The lead is Taste Asian Food (4.5 from 41): mango puree, a little cream and milk, sugar and gelatin, chilled at least 2 hours, topped with milk and mango cubes. Gelatin is not vegetarian, so agar replaces it, as Teak & Thyme (5 from 7) suggests; agar sets firmer and faster, and it has to be boiled to dissolve. The lead's coconut milk and mint garnish are left out, and a milk topping is used (the lead allows either). Eat the leftover mango as it is.
